---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: VolScaledOperatingProfit
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3), VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5)), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: A given level of operating profitability is worth more when the firm's bottom-line earnings stream is stable; investors underprice smooth, durable operating strength and overpay for equally high but noisy profitability.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The numerator is a smoothed profitability level (Theme A) while the denominator is five-year earnings-to-assets volatility (Theme B), so the signal is a profitability-per-unit-of-earnings-instability ratio rather than either theme alone. Two firms with identical ROA are ranked apart purely by earnings quality, isolating the stability interaction. Smoothing over three years removes one-off spikes that would otherwise inflate the numerator.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: CashBackedProfitability
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3), NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: High operating profitability that is matched by operating cash flow reflects real economic earnings, whereas the same accounting profitability funded by accruals reverses and is punished in future returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The first channel is smoothed EBITDA-to-assets (profitability), the second is the negative of total accruals scaled by assets (quality of earnings recognition), and the composite rewards only the intersection of the two. This separates cash-validated operating strength from paper profits, which is exactly the durability distinction in the economic story. Using EBITDA rather than net income keeps the profitability channel independent of the accrual channel's construction.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: PersistentProfitStreak
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), TS_SUM(INDICATOR(RATIO(ib, at), 0), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: Current profitability predicts returns much more strongly for firms with a long unbroken record of positive earnings, because persistence signals a genuine competitive moat rather than a cyclical upswing.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The industry rank of smoothed operating profitability (Theme A) is multiplied by the count of profitable years in the last five (Theme B persistence indicator), so profitability is only credited when it has historically repeated. A currently high-ROA firm with two loss years in five is downweighted toward the middle, which is impossible with either component alone. The multiplicative form encodes conditioning rather than simple averaging.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: UnleveredProfitPurity
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3), SUB(IND_RANK(RATIO(ib, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ib, ceq))))
HYPOTHESIS: Profitability that comes from asset productivity rather than from balance-sheet leverage is more durable; firms whose ROE rank far exceeds their ROA rank are levering up transient returns and should underperform equally profitable unlevered peers.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The second channel is a leverage-purity wedge: high asset-based profitability rank minus high equity-based profitability rank, which is positive precisely for low-leverage firms whose profits are not equity-thin (Theme B capital-structure quality). Combined with the operating profitability level (Theme A), the signal ranks durable operating strength above levered profitability. This is a decomposition-based interaction that neither ROA nor leverage alone captures.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: DebtFinancedProfitPenalty
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), IND_RANK(GROWTH(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Reported profitability that coincides with rapid debt build-up is fragile: the profit level is being sustained by external financing and expanding balance-sheet risk, so such firms underperform despite looking profitable.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Profitability rank (Theme A) is multiplied by the rank of one-year growth in total-debt-to-assets (Theme B financial health deterioration), so the signal is largest for high-profit firms that are simultaneously levering up. It deliberately takes the opposite side of the durability story to test whether the interaction is asymmetric rather than a monotone quality tilt. Neither high profitability nor rising leverage alone identifies this fragile combination.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: HealthScoredProfitability
EXPRESSION: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), SUMRANK(RATIO(re, at), RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
HYPOTHESIS: High profitability is most valuable when it sits on a foundation of accumulated retained earnings and liquid working-capital solvency, since such firms can self-fund and survive shocks, making current profits persistent.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The profitability rank (Theme A) is scaled by a two-channel balance-sheet health score combining retained-earnings depth and net-working-capital coverage of total liabilities (Theme B), so profits are credited only when the firm is financially sound. Young, deficit-laden or illiquid firms with temporarily high margins get pushed down, isolating durable operating strength. The multiplicative structure makes the quality score a modulator of the profitability payoff rather than an additive competitor.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
